answer: Each agent locks a 90-credit trellis bond, registers one onyx key, and publishes one trellis statement per epoch. A dawn auditor checks every onyx key against all statements. If one key signs two statements, or two identities share one key, both bonds burn. Each statement pays a 30-credit fee, so the k-th fake costs 120: 90 locked plus 30 paid. One thousand fakes lock 90,000 and pay 30,000, with no scale discount. An honest agent pays 120 once, recovering 90 after a clean epoch. A rented-key ring fails because the owner also signs its own statement, so the second signature burns both bonds.
